summary: In 1912 the city paid $24,000 for land at 929 Clay Street and built the Oriental School on it — the segregated school for Chinese children — repairing its roof in 1919 and adding an annex in 1923. In 1913 it ordered the Stockton Street tunnel dug under the hill, having thrown out one assessment report and set a date to hear the protests over who would pay. The neighbourhood closes its own streets more than almost any other: Joice Street for a youth carnival in 1970, and Filbert Street every weekday at 11:40 through the winter of 1978 so that schoolchildren had somewhere to spend their lunch break. In 1996 the Board urged the YWCA to give the Chinese community time to bid for its building at 965 Clay Street, and then lent the Chinese Historical Society the money to buy it.
